Six friends, G, H, I, J, K, and L, are sitting around a circular table, facing towards the centre of the table.
1) H is sitting third to the left of G.
2) L and I are not neighbours of H.
3) K is sitting to the immediate right of I.
Therefore, 'J' is sitting to the immediate left of 'L'.

questions.question:
Which number breaks the sequence?

5, 7, 10, 15, 23, 33, 46
questions.solution:
The sequence should follow consecutive prime-number increments.

5 + 2 = 7
7 + 3 = 10
10 + 5 = 15
15 + 7 = 22
22 + 11 = 33
33 + 13 = 46

So, 23 should be replaced by 22.

Hence, 23 breaks the sequence.

questions.question:
Which number breaks the sequence?

6, 14, 31, 67, 140, 293
questions.solution:
The sequence should follow: multiply by 2 and add consecutive prime numbers.
6 × 2 + 2 = 14
14 × 2 + 3 = 31
31 × 2 + 5 = 67
67 × 2 + 7 = 141
141 × 2 + 11 = 293

So, 140 should be replaced by 141.

Hence, 140 breaks the sequence.

questions.question:
Here some problem or solution of the problem is given in the statement you have to choose the appropriate logical deduction for given statement.

Statement:

A city increased bus frequency on two overcrowded corridors and introduced a single smart pass usable on buses and metro. After these changes, average waiting time for buses on those corridors fell, and transfers to metro increased. Air-quality readings near those corridors improved, but the report states that the improvement was no more than 6% compared to the previous quarter.

Conclusions:

I. The air-quality improvement near those corridors was less than 6%.

II. Integrated passes and higher bus frequency can increase bus-to-metro transfers.

III. The smart pass is the only reason for the improvement in air quality.

Which conclusion(s) necessarily follow(s)?
questions.solution:
Conclusion I does not follow because "no more than 6%" allows exactly 6%, so "less than 6%" is not guaranteed.

Conclusion II follows because the statement directly says transfers to metro increased after these changes.

Conclusion III does not follow because the improvement in air quality could be due to higher bus frequency (reducing car trips), the smart pass, or both. The statement does not establish the smart pass as the sole cause.

In this question, two statements I and II have been given. These statements may be independent causes or effects of independent causes or a common cause. One of the statements maybe the effect of the other statement. Read all statements and select the correct answer.

I. Shop X launches a scheme where an individual has to pay monthly installments continuously for 11 months and the 1-month installment will be paid by the firm. Post completion of the scheme period, an individual can purchase gold jewellery of the total amount accumulated in his account.

options.a: I is the cause and II is its possible effect
options.b: II is a cause and I is its possible effect
options.c: Both I and II are effects of a common cause
options.d: Both I and II are effects of independent causes

questions.solution:
Both statements I and II share a common background.

Shop X introduces a scheme in which a customer has to pay 11 consecutive monthly installment payments; the company will cover one month's payment. An individual can use the entire amount accumulated in his account to purchase gold jewelry after the scheme has ended. So, I is the cause and II is its possible effect.

questions.question:
If 'A' denotes 'addition', 'B' denotes 'multiplication', 'C' denotes 'subtraction', and 'D' denotes 'division', then what will be the value of the following expression?
72 D 6 B 12 A 24 C 18 C (20 B 5 A 48)
Options:
A: 1
B: 3
C: 2
D: 4
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:
By using BODMAS RULE:
The given information is:
A -> +
B -> ×
C -> -
D -> ÷
Given expression is: 72 ÷ 6 × 12 + 24 - 18 - (20 × 5 + 48)
= 72 ÷ 6 × 12 + 24 - 18 - (100 + 48)
= 72 ÷ 6 × 12 + 24 - 18 - 148
= 12 × 12 + 24 - 18 - 148
= 144 + 24 - 18 - 148
= 168 - 18 - 148
= 168 - 166
= 2
Hence, the correct answer is "2".

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.
Statements:
Some Bangles are Bracelets.
All chains are Rings.
Some Bracelets are Chains.
Conclusions:
(I) Some Bangles are Rings.
(II) Some Chains are Bangles.
(III) Some Rings are Bracelets.
Options:
A: Only Conclusion III follows.
B: Both Conclusions I and II follow.
C: Both Conclusions I and III follow.
D: Only Conclusion I follows.

options.b: Both Conclusions I and II follow.
options.c: Both Conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:
I. Some Bangles are Rings → Does not Follow (As some bangles are bracelets, some bracelets are chains and all chains are rings. So, it is possible but not definitely true)
II. Some Chains are Bangles → Does not Follow (As some bangles are bracelets, some bracelets are chains and all chains are rings. So, it is possible but not definitely true)
III. Some Rings are Bracelets → Follow (As some bracelets are chains and all chains are rings. So, as whole chains comes in rings which some part comes in bracelets therefore it is definitely true)
∴ Here, Only Conclusion III follows.
Hence, the correct answer is "Only Conclusion III follows".

questions.question: In a row of children facing north, A is 14th from the left end and 6th to the right of B. If B is 15th to the left of C, who is 22nd from the right end, how many children are there in that row?
questions.solution:
Here, A is 14th from the left end and 6th to the right of B. Hence, B is 14 - 6 = 8th from the left side.
Again, B is 15th to the left of C, who is 22nd from the right end.
Hence, B is 15 + 22 = 37th from the right side.
Therefore, the total number of children
= B's position from the right end + B's position from the left end - 1
= 37 + 8 - 1 = 45 - 1 = 44
Hence, option B is correct answer.

16 : 96

And,
18 : 120
[18 × (18 + 2)] ÷ 3 = 120 
[18 × (18 + 2)] = 120 × 3
18 × 20 = 360
360 = 360 (LHS = RHS)

Similarly,
? : 161
Let '?' be 'x'
x × (x + 2) = 161 × 3
x^2 + 2x = 483
x^2 + 2x - 483 = 0 
x^2 + 23x - 21x - 483 = 0
(x + 23) (x - 21) = 0
x = either -23 or 21

As, the answer cannot be negative, therefore value of x will be 21.
Hence, "21" is the correct answer.

The greatest decimal number = 0.8678
The smallest decimal number = 0.05989
So, the required difference = 0.8678 - 0.05989 = 0.80791

questions.question:
Select the option in which the words in the word-pair share the same relationship as that shares by the given word-pair.
Tiger: Felidae
questions.solution:
The logic is:
Tiger: Felidae → Tiger belongs to the family of Felidae.
Similarly,
1) Lion: Leporidae → Lion belongs to the family of Felidae.
2) Rabbit: Bovidae → Rabbit belongs to the family of Leporidae.
3) Whale: Cetacea → Whale belongs to the family of Cetacea
4) Elephant: Canidae → Elephant belongs to the family of Elephantidae.
Hence, 'Whale: Cetacea' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which of the two digits should be interchanged to correct the following equation?
75 ÷ 18 + 51 × 8 - 82 = 87
questions.solution:
Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) 7 & 8
Given: 75 ÷ 18 + 51 × 8 - 82 = 87
After interchanging the digit we get;
⇒ 85 ÷ 17 + 51 × 7 - 72 = 87
⇒ 5 + 51 × 7 - 72 = 87
⇒ 5 + 357 - 72 = 87
⇒ 362 - 72 = 87
⇒ 290 ≠ 87

Option 2) 1 & 5
Given: 75 ÷ 18 + 51 × 8 - 82 = 87
After interchanging the digit we get;
⇒ 71 ÷ 58 + 15 × 8 - 82 = 87
⇒ 1.22 + 15 × 8 - 82 = 87
⇒ 39.22 ≠ 87

Option 3) 5 & 2
Given: 75 ÷ 18 + 51 × 8 - 82 = 87
After interchanging the digit we get;
⇒ 72 ÷ 18 + 21 × 8 - 85 = 87
⇒ 4 + 21 × 8 - 85 = 87
⇒ 4 + 168 - 85 = 87
⇒ 172 - 85 = 87
⇒ 87 = 87
⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) 8 & 2
Given: 75 ÷ 18 + 51 × 8 - 82 = 87
After interchanging the digit we get;
⇒ 75 ÷ 12 + 51 × 2 - 28 = 87
⇒ 80.25 ≠ 87

Hence, the correct answer is "5 & 2".

questions.question:
Statement: The richer we are the more self-centered we become and neglect other's needs.
Conclusions:
I. All rich are self-centered.
II. Those who neglect other's needs are rich.

options.c: Both I and II are true.
options.d: Neither I nor II is true.

questions.solution:
The statement shares an idea that the richer a person gets the more self-centered he becomes and ignores others.
From what is supplied it cannot be concluded that all the rich are self-centered. This is a generic conclusion and may not hold true for all the rich. Therefore conclusion I does not follow.
Also from the supplied statement, we cannot conclude the converse that those who are selfish and neglect other's needs are necessarily rich. Therefore, conclusion II does not follow.
Hence, neither conclusion I nor II is true.

questions.question:
If in the number sequence 8 3 2 1 6 2 4 3 7 1 7 2 all the odd numbers are increased by two and all the even numbers are decreased by two, then the new number sequence is arranged in ascending order, which will be the fifth number from the left?
Options:
A: 3
B: 2
C: 4
D: 5
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:
Given number sequence 8 3 2 1 6 2 4 3 7 1 7 2.
Now, all the odd numbers are increased by two and all the even numbers are decreased by two
The number sequence (8 – 2) (3 + 2) (2 – 2) (1 + 2) (6 – 2) (2 – 2) (4 – 2) (3 + 2) (7 + 2) (1 + 2) (7 + 2) (2 – 2)
Or, 6 5 0 3 4 0 2 5 9 3 9 0
Then the new number sequence is arranged in ascending order;
0 0 0 2 3 3 4 5 5 6 9 9
Therefore, the fifth number from the left is '3'.
Hence, the correct answer is '3'.

questions.question: Sum of ages of father and son is 8 years more than the age of mother. Son was born when the mother was 22 years. How old is the father?
questions.solution:
Let the age of father be F, son be S and mother be M.
Sum of ages of father and son is 8 years more than the age of mother.
F + S = M + 8
Son was born when the mother was 22 years.
So, when M = 22, S = 0
F + 0 = 22 + 8
=> F = 30
Hence, '30 years' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.
Statements:
No plate is Mug.
Some Mugs are Tables.
Conclusions:
I. All plates being tables is a possibility.
II. Some tables are not mugs.

options.a: Both conclusions I and II follow
options.b: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:
No plate is Mug.
Some Mugs are Tables.
Conclusions:
I. All plates being tables is a possibility - True (Because, No definite relation given between plates and tables, so All plates being tables can be possible).
II. Some tables are not mugs - False (Because, Some tables are mugs, but no information given to the remaining part, so only possibility can be true here).
So, Only conclusion I follows.
Hence, the correct answer is Option C.

questions.question:
In the question below, a statement followed by two conclusions numbered I and II is given. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true, then consider the two conclusions together and decide which of them logically follows beyond a reasonable doubt from the information given in the statement.
Statement : If all players play to their full potential, we will win the match. We have won the match.
Conclusions :
I. All players played to their full potential.
II. Some players did not play to their full potential.
questions.solution:
Given:
Statement: If all players play to their full potential, we will win the match. We have won the match.
Conclusions:
I. All players played to their full potential - False (Because the statement is of the form If P, then Q. From the fact that Q has occurred (we won the match), it cannot be concluded that P must have occurred.)
II. Some players did not play to their full potential - False (Because there is no information to conclude this.)

So, neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Neither I nor II follows".
